London, 27<sup>th</sup> February 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**For Pan African Resources** , the proposed acquisition of Phoenix Platinum from Metorex would be an important part of its future expansion plans, CEO Jan Nelson said today.  The company sees Phoenix, which owns platinum-bearing waste dumps in South Africa, as an “exciting” prospect.  Given the current economic climate, Pan African had advanced to projects that were at the prefeasibility stage or at nearterm production stage and away from grassroots projects.  Earlier this month, Pan African announced that it had entered into an exclusive agreement with Metorex, which owned a controlling stake in the junior miner, to acquire Phoenix Platinum, which owns certain rights to the contained PGMs from both surface tailings dumps and operating mines in South Africa’s Bushveld Complex.  Nelson reported that the estimated capital expenditure on the Phoenix project would be about £6,9-million, most of which could be recovered within the first full year of production.  The project’s life-of-mine is reported to be five to seven years based on the current surface tailings and about 18 years from underground mining. Pan African plans to use a significant portion of the profits that could be generated from the Phoenix project to fund future acquisitions, Nelson noted. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Toyota** led the biggest decline in Japan auto production on record. Output by the country’s 12 automakers fell 41 % to 576,539 vehicles in January from a year earlier, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association said, the biggest drop since the group started tracking y-o-y declines in 1967. Exports fell 59 %, the most since at least 1973. Exports to all major regions fell, led by a 77 % plunge for those to the U.S.  Toyota’s domestic output plunged 40 %, the most in more than two decades, to 209,224 vehicles and its exports to the U.S. sank 80 %. Japan’s overall exports plunged 46 % in January, resulting in a record trade deficit, the Finance Ministry said earlier this week. Vehicle sales in the country fell the most in 35 years last month. U.S. industrywide auto sales may hit a 27- year low of 10.5 million vehicles this year, according to General Motors.  Japan’s auto exports fell to 233,859 vehicles in January. Shipments to Europe followed the U.S. lower, plunging 63 %, and those to Asia dropped 55 %. Toyota, on Feb. 6 tripled its loss forecast to 450 billion yen ($4.6 billion) as auto sales plummet and a surging yen cuts the value of overseas sales. Honda said domestic output fell 23 % to 77,224 units as shipments to the U.S. tanked 62 % and those to Asia sank 57 %.  Japan output at Nissan dropped 59 % to 47,477 units, led by a 85 % decline in exports to North America. _Source: Bloomberg_ 

**The European Union** would consider appealing to the World Trade Organisation if U.S. aid for the American auto industry made conditions unfair for European manufacturers, the EU’s transport chie

f Antonio Tajani said.  The EU car industry has warned that output could fall by at least 15 % this year and producers might need up to 15 billion euros ($19.10 billion) in financial help.  Already car industry support schemes within France, Spain, Britain, Italy, German and Sweden are being scrutinised by EU competition authorities.   Tajani also pointed out an imbalance in auto sector trade with South Korea, saying the EU should only go ahead with a trade deal with Seoul “if we also get some advantages”. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**The Environmental Protection Agency** was ordered by a federal circuit court to review limits on particulate air pollution, who said that the agency failed to adequately explain its decision not to tighten those limits. 

_Source:  Morning Star_ 

**Nymex** Platinum inventories reached a twelve year high level at end-Jan 09, reaching 2.8 tonnes. Palladium stocks stood at 13 tonnes.
